title: Review: Simple harmonic motion; Wave model

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Frequency, f
items.clue: The number of complete oscillations per unit time.

items.label: Amplitude
items.clue: The maximum displacement of a particle of the medium from its equilibrium position.

items.label: Displacement, x
items.clue: The distance of the oscillating body from its equilibrium position, in a stated direction.

items.label: Travelling (progressive) wave
items.clue: A disturbance that moves through a medium or through space and transfers energy from one place to another.

questions.stem: A long simple pendulum hangs in the stairwell of a school. Swinging with a small amplitude, its bob takes 2.10 s to move from one extreme position to the other. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the length of the pendulum?
questions.explanation: One extreme to the other is half an oscillation, so T = 2 × 2.10 = 4.20 s. l = gT²/(4π²) = 9.8 × 4.20² / (4π²) = 4.38 m.

questions.stem: The displacement of an undamped oscillator varies sinusoidally with time, with time period T. Which statement describes how the kinetic energy of the oscillator varies with time?

options.text: It rises and falls once in each period, in step with the displacement.
It is greatest at zero displacement, with two maxima in each period.
It is greatest at each extreme displacement, where the acceleration is greatest.
It varies between negative and positive values, just as the velocity does.

questions.explanation: Kinetic energy depends on the speed, which is greatest at equilibrium. The oscillator passes through equilibrium twice per cycle, once in each direction, so the kinetic energy reaches its maximum twice in each period.

questions.stem: A simple pendulum swings with a small amplitude and time period T. Its bob is replaced by one of twice the mass, keeping the same length from the point of suspension to the centre of the bob. The new pendulum is set swinging with twice the original amplitude, which is still small. What is the new time period?

options.text: It is less than T, as a heavier bob is pulled more strongly and swings faster.
It is unchanged at T, as for small amplitudes the period depends only on l and g.
It is more than T, as the bob now travels twice as far in each oscillation.
It is √2 × T, as the period of any oscillator is proportional to √m.

questions.stem: A body is displaced from its equilibrium position and released. Which condition ensures that it then moves with simple harmonic motion?

options.text: A resultant force of constant size acts on it, directed towards the equilibrium position.
The resultant force on it is proportional to its displacement and acts in the same direction as it.
It moves back and forth along the same path, taking the same time for each cycle.
The resultant force on it is proportional to its displacement and directed towards equilibrium.

questions.explanation: This is the condition for SHM. The size of the resultant force is proportional to the displacement from equilibrium, and its direction is always towards equilibrium, so a = −ω²x.

questions.stem: A body moves with simple harmonic motion along a horizontal line with angular frequency 4.0 rad s⁻¹. Displacements to the right of the equilibrium position are positive. The body is released from rest 0.050 m to the right of the equilibrium position. What is its acceleration when it has moved 0.020 m from the point of release?
A particle moves with simple harmonic motion. Which statement about the quantities used to describe its motion is correct?

options.text: The amplitude is greatest at each extreme and zero when the particle is at equilibrium.
The equilibrium position is where the particle is momentarily at rest in each cycle.
Displacement is measured from equilibrium and is negative for half of each cycle.
The time period is the time taken to move from one extreme to the other.

questions.explanation: Displacement is measured from equilibrium and is signed. The particle spends half of each cycle on each side of equilibrium, so its displacement is positive for half the cycle and negative for the other half.

questions.stem: A mass hanging from a spring oscillates with simple harmonic motion with an angular frequency of 40.0 rad s⁻¹. What is the time period of the oscillation?
questions.explanation: One oscillation corresponds to 2π rad of phase, so T = 2π/ω = 2π/40.0 = 0.157 s. Equivalently f = ω/2π = 6.37 Hz and T = 1/f = 0.157 s.

questions.stem: A trolley hung from a newton meter gives a reading of 14.7 N. The trolley is then attached to a spring system on a horizontal track and oscillates with negligible friction. The spring constant of the system is 7.50 N m⁻¹. Take g = 9.8 m s⁻². What is the time period of the oscillation?
The time period of a simple pendulum is given by T = 2π√(l/g). Which condition must be met for this equation to give an accurate value?

options.text: The amplitude can be of any size, since the period is independent of the amplitude.
The bob must be light, as a heavier bob is pulled harder and swings faster than predicted.
The bob swings with a regular period, which makes its motion simple harmonic.
The amplitude is small, so the restoring force is close to proportional to displacement.

questions.stem: A mass on a horizontal spring moves with simple harmonic motion on a frictionless surface; air resistance is negligible. Which statement about the energy of the oscillator is correct?

options.text: At each extreme, E_k is greatest, because the acceleration of the mass is greatest there.
At each extreme, the total energy is zero, because the mass is not moving there.
At each extreme, all the energy is stored in the spring, because the mass is at rest.
The total energy falls during each cycle, because energy is used up in keeping the mass moving.

questions.stem: A longitudinal wave travels in the +x direction along a slinky spring. Displacements of the coils in the +x direction are positive. At one instant, the graph of displacement s against equilibrium position x is a sine curve: s = 0 at x = 0, s = +3.0 mm at x = 10 cm, s = 0 at x = 20 cm, s = −3.0 mm at x = 30 cm and s = 0 at x = 40 cm. Where, between x = 0 and x = 40 cm, is the centre of a compression?

options.text: At x = 10 cm, where the displacement is greatest and positive
At x = 10 cm and x = 30 cm, where s has its greatest magnitude
At x = 20 cm, where coils on both sides are displaced towards it
At x = 0, 20 cm and 40 cm, where the displacement s is zero

questions.stem: A transverse wave travels along a stretched string. Adjacent crests are 1.2 m apart. A graph of displacement y against time t for one point on the string is a sine curve: y = 0 at t = 0, y is a maximum at t = 5 ms, y = 0 at t = 10 ms, y is a minimum at t = 15 ms and y = 0 at t = 20 ms, after which the pattern repeats. What is the wave speed?

options.text: 120 m s⁻¹
60 m s⁻¹

questions.explanation: One full oscillation (maximum, zero, minimum, back to zero) takes T = 20 ms = 0.020 s, and λ = 1.2 m. v = λ/T = 1.2 m ÷ 0.020 s = 60 m s⁻¹.
